title: An agent tool call fails inside an automated workflow. Which failure class should trigger automated exponential backoff with jitter in the harness, rather than immediate failure or feeding the error back to the LLM?

An HTTP tool wrapper uses a 4.0-second per-attempt timeout and up to 3 total attempts (1 initial call plus 2 retries), with deterministic backoff sleeps of 1.0 s after attempt 1 and 2.0 s after attempt 2 (no sleep after the final failure). If every attempt hangs until its timeout fires, what is the worst-case elapsed time in seconds for that single tool step?

Why must an agent harness bind an idempotency key to the logical step `(run_id, step_seq, tool_name, args_hash)` before network dispatch, rather than generating a fresh UUID inside the HTTP retry helper or reusing one static key per user?

A multi-step agent checkpoints after every completed step. After executing `charge_card($50)` on step 4, the worker crashes before persisting step 4's completion marker. On restart from step 3, the supervisor re-invokes the LLM to generate step 4 again; the LLM picks slightly different wording (`memo: "Order retry"`), generating a different argument hash, bypassing the idempotency cache, and double-charging the customer. What durable-execution invariant failed?

During a partial database brownout, a three-layer stack runs independent retries: the root supervisor retries a failing sub-agent up to 3 times (4 total tries), the sub-agent's tool client retries a flaky internal service up to 3 times (4 total tries), and that internal service retries its database query up to 2 times (3 total tries). For 1 user request when every call stalls, how many total database attempts can this stack emit?

Your ops agent calls `create_ticket(priority="high")`, gets a schema rejection from a downstream validator, self-corrects to `priority="urgent"`, and accidentally reuses the previous step's `idempotency_key`. The server returns HTTP 200 with the original response (`priority="high"`), leaving the agent convinced its correction succeeded. What two bugs caused this?

A 50-step autonomous coding workflow runs at 4.0 seconds per step. Saving a durable state checkpoint after every step adds 0.5 seconds overhead per step (25.0 s total across 50 steps). Suppose a worker preemption hits once right after step 25 finishes: without checkpoints, the run restarts from step 0 (re-running 25 steps); with per-step checkpoints, recovery resumes immediately at step 26 with 0 lost steps. How many net seconds does per-step checkpointing save on this preempted run?

An async agent worker pulls a malformed webhook event containing invalid UTF-8 bytes, crashes with an unhandled `UnicodeDecodeError` before acking the message, and restarts. The queue immediately redelivers the same message to the next pod, and within 5 minutes every worker pod is stuck crash-looping. Diagnose and fix this poison-pill failure.

A background agent worker picks up a 10-minute database backfill tool job from a queue configured with a 60-second visibility timeout and no heartbeats. At second 61, the broker marks the task stalled and hands it to Worker B, so two workers run the same non-atomic migration concurrently. How do you stop split-brain execution?

Why does appending full raw stack traces from four failed tool retries directly into an agent's active message history degrade accuracy on step 5, and how should the harness surface retry failures instead?

You ship a breaking refactor to your agent workflow—renaming a tool and splitting a single `plan` state node into `draft_plan` and `verify_plan`—while 2,000 long-running agent runs are checkpointed in `AWAITING_APPROVAL`. How do you resume all 2,000 runs cleanly without deserialization crashes?

Design a durable checkpoint-and-recovery engine for a multi-step enterprise agent executing mixed external APIs—some idempotent (Stripe), some non-idempotent legacy SOAP/SMTP endpoints—in an environment with 30-second spot-instance preemption notices.

An agent finishes a customer support task with the exact right final refund amount, yet its execution trace shows it ignored an internal policy cache, queried an admin-only table twice, and retried 11 turns to get there. Why must agent evaluation grade trajectory alongside end-state outcome?

A customer-refund agent succeeds independently on 85% of trials (`p = 0.85`). Enterprise release criteria evaluate `pass^k`, requiring all `k = 4` independent trials on a scenario to pass without failure. What is `pass^4` as a percentage? (One decimal.)

Why do agent benchmarks like tau-bench and SWE-bench grade the final mutated environment state (database diffs or unit-test suites) rather than scoring the agent's final natural-language message against a reference string?

In an OpenTelemetry-instrumented agent runtime, why must LLM generations, tool invocations, and sub-agent calls share a single root `trace_id` with parent-child `span_id` links rather than emitting flat independent HTTP logs?

Compare running agent CI evaluations against deterministic recorded tool stubs (VCR mocks) versus live ephemeral sandboxes (seeded containers and mock servers). When do VCR mocks give dangerous false confidence?

On a 500-task evaluation suite, Agent V1 solves 80% of tasks (400 tasks), averaging $0.06 per successful trajectory and $0.14 per failed trajectory (where the remaining 100 runs exhaust the turn cap). What is the effective cost per resolved task (`total spend ÷ resolved tasks`) in USD? (Three decimals.)

Your billing agent fails 32% of multi-step refund tasks. Reading only final outputs makes every failure look like the LLM hallucinated refund amounts—yet step-by-step traces show `lookup_order` returned stale cached rows on step 2 before step 3 computed the refund. What evaluation taxonomy fix separates these failures?

Your conversational agent scores 94% completion against an LLM user simulator in staging, yet drops to 61% during live customer beta. Inspecting transcripts shows the simulator always answers clarifying questions clearly, copies exact IDs verbatim, and never reverses itself mid-conversation. Diagnose the gap and fix it.

An agent benchmark runs 400 evaluation tasks. Exactly 300 runs pass the final database end-state verification, yet trajectory trace auditing flags that 15% of those 300 passing runs violated a safety or tool policy (calling an unapproved admin read or bypassing confirmation). What is the true policy-compliant pass rate across all 400 tasks, in percent? (Two decimals.)

Your 100-task agent eval suite fails PR CI randomly 35% of the time on completely unchanged commits, causing engineers to ignore red builds and hit retry. Why does a naive single-run threshold fail on multi-step agents, and how do you make CI deterministic and reliable?

Design an automated production trace-to-eval flywheel that mines live agent OpenTelemetry traces for novel failures, strips PII, and turns them into regression tests without bloating CI or overfitting stale traffic.

Design an evaluation harness for a hierarchical multi-agent system (Lead Planner, Research Worker, Code-Execution Worker) that isolates component regressions, preserves cross-agent traces, and resets shared state cleanly.
A decision tree with no depth limit scores 99% on training data and 71% on validation. What do you try first?
A 10-class image classifier gets 64% on training data and 63% on validation. People score 95% on the same task. What's the problem?
You run 5-fold cross-validation on 10,000 rows. How many rows does each of the five models train on?
A demand forecast scores 0.92 R² with random 5-fold cross-validation and 0.55 in its first month in production. What's the most likely cause?
In a churn model, the most important feature by far is `account_closure_reason`. Validation AUC is 0.99. What do you conclude?
A colleague oversamples the minority class with SMOTE, then splits the data into train and test. Test recall is excellent. What's wrong?
Out of 1,000 transactions, 20 are fraud. Your model flags 50 transactions, and 15 of those are fraud. What is its precision?
Same model: 20 frauds in the data, 15 of them flagged. What is its recall?
Same model, precision 0.3 and recall 0.75. What is its F1 score? (Three decimals is fine.)
1% of users are fraudulent and your model has 99% accuracy. What should you report instead?
A test catches 99% of a rare condition and wrongly flags 1% of healthy people. The condition affects 1 in 1,000. If someone tests positive, what's the probability they have it? (As a decimal.)
The fraud team can review 200 cases a day. How do you choose the model's threshold?
Your model has a ROC-AUC of 0.95, and its predicted probabilities will be used to set insurance prices. What else do you check?
A model predicts 0.9 for an example that turns out positive. What is the log loss for that one prediction? (Natural log.)
You have 500 features and suspect only about 20 matter. You want a linear model that uses few of them. Which regularisation?
Your features range from 0–1 (a ratio) to 0–1,000,000 (income). Which of these models doesn't care about the difference in scale?
A random forest's built-in feature importance ranks `zip_code` (30,000 distinct values) at the top. Should you believe it?
k-nearest neighbours works well on 5 features but poorly once you add 195 more mostly-irrelevant ones. Why?
Two features in a linear regression have a correlation of 0.98. Their coefficients flip sign between training runs on resampled data. What's happening?
Income is missing for 30% of loan applicants, and applicants with missing income default twice as often. How do you handle it?
A model's real-world performance seems to have dropped, but true labels arrive 30 days late. What can you monitor today?
A feature has two buckets. In training, 30% of rows fall in bucket A and 70% in B. This week it's 70% A and 30% B. What's the population stability index (PSI)? (Natural log.)
An A/B test: control converts 10% of 5,000 users, the variant converts 11% of 5,000. What's the two-proportion z-score? (Two decimals.)
A product manager checks the A/B dashboard every morning and plans to stop the test the first day p is below 0.05. What's the problem?
A freshly initialised 10-class classifier should predict roughly uniform probabilities. What cross-entropy loss should you see on the very first batch? (Natural log.)
Training loss sits at 2.30 for a 10-class problem and doesn't move for 1,000 steps. What's your first debugging step?
Training loss keeps falling. Validation loss falls until epoch 5, then rises every epoch. What's happening, and what do you do?
Loss jumps up and down by a lot from step to step and doesn't trend down. What do you change first?
Training in fp16, the loss suddenly becomes NaN after 200 steps. What's the most likely cause?
Evaluating the same checkpoint twice on the same validation set gives 81.2% and then 79.6%. What did you forget?
The learning rate warms up linearly from 0 to 3e-4 over the first 2,000 steps. What is it at step 500?
After warmup, the learning rate follows a cosine decay from 3e-4 down to 0 over the remaining steps. What is it exactly halfway through the decay?
Why do most transformer fine-tuning recipes use AdamW rather than Adam with an L2 penalty added to the loss?
You raise the batch size from 256 to 1,024 on the same SGD setup. What's a common starting point for the learning rate?
A transformer trains well but the loss spikes sharply every few thousand steps, then slowly recovers. What's a standard fix?
With He initialisation for a ReLU layer that has 512 inputs, what is the standard deviation of the initial weights? (Three decimals.)
You train a segmentation model with batch norm, and memory limits you to 2 images per GPU. Results are poor and noisy. Why, and what do you do?
A plain 50-layer network trains worse than an 18-layer one, even on the training set. What's the usual fix?
How many parameters are in a fully connected layer from 4,096 inputs to 4,096 outputs, with a bias?
A 3×3 convolution takes 64 input channels to 128 output channels, with a bias. How many parameters?
How much GPU memory do the weights alone of a 7-billion-parameter model take in bf16? (In GB, where 1 GB is 10⁹ bytes.)

Training that 7B model with Adam in mixed precision: bf16 weights and gradients (2 bytes each), plus fp32 master weights and Adam's two moments (4 bytes each). How much memory before activations? (GB, 10⁹ bytes.)
Training runs out of memory at batch size 32. You want to keep an effective batch of 32. What do you do?
Each GPU processes a micro-batch of 8, you accumulate gradients over 16 micro-batches, and you train on 4 GPUs with data parallelism. What's the effective batch size?
You need to train on 1 billion tokens. Each GPU processes 50,000 tokens a second, and you have 8 of them. How many minutes does one pass take, ignoring overheads?
Why do most large-model training runs now use bf16 rather than fp16?
An image classifier scores 98% on validation and 81% on new photos. You find that augmented copies of the same originals appear in both the training and validation sets. What's the fix?
Your extraction pipeline uses plain JSON mode, yet downstream code fails with KeyError on 4% of invoices. Why does switching to strict JSON Schema enforcement fix this?
A strict JSON Schema guarantees every field parses without error, yet analysts still find wrong numbers in 6% of extracted contracts. Why does schema enforcement not prevent this?

Constrained JSON decoding inserts 28 formatting tokens (braces, keys, quotes) per record alongside 12 content tokens. On 50,000 daily records at $4.00 per million output tokens, what is the monthly (30-day) output cost of the formatting tokens alone? (USD.)
A strict-schema extraction call suddenly returns `Unterminated string` in `json.loads` on 3% of long customer emails. The provider returned HTTP 200. What do you inspect first?
Your structured ticket classifier gets 92% accuracy in staging, yet in production it assigns `billing_dispute` to 68% of unrelated tickets after you add four few-shot examples. What caused the skew?

An unconstrained extraction prompt passes Pydantic validation on 85% of first attempts, and each independent retry (up to 3 total attempts) also passes with probability 0.85. What percentage of requests still fail after 3 attempts? (Two decimals.)
After enabling dynamic regex-constrained JSON schemas per user request on your vLLM cluster, p99 time-to-first-token spikes from 180 ms to 2.4 s while GPU utilization drops. What is the bottleneck?

Your structured output schema forces the model to emit `decision` (`approve` or `reject`) as the first JSON key, and accuracy on complex claims drops 11 points compared to free text. How do you redesign the schema?

A structured extractor uses jump-forward grammar decoding: an average JSON output has 60 tokens total, of which 24 deterministic boilerplate tokens skip GPU decode passes, and 36 tokens take 18 ms/token on GPU. Including a fixed 90 ms prefill and 15 ms schema lookup, what is the end-to-end latency in ms?

You enforce strict JSON output via `response_format` on a chat model that also has two callable tools. Suddenly the model stops invoking tools and prints tool-call JSON inside the user-facing response. Why, and how do you fix it?
Design a strict-schema clinical entity extractor for messy doctor notes where 40% of fields are genuinely absent in any given note, without inducing fabricated defaults.
Design a real-time UI that streams structured JSON fields (`title`, `bullets`, `confidence`) to users under 300 ms TTFT while guaranteeing final schema validity and preventing partial-field XSS.

Against the reference "Refunds arrive within 5 business days", Model A outputs "Money is returned in five working days" and Model B outputs "Refunds arrive within 30 business days". Why do BLEU and ROUGE-L score Model B far higher?

Your QA evaluator uses raw string equality (`pred == ref`) and reports 41% accuracy on a model that human raters score at 78%. What normalization bugs cause this gap, and where can normalization go too far?
Using the unbiased `pass@k` estimator `1 - comb(n - c, k) / comb(n, k)`, you draw n = 10 samples for a coding task and c = 2 pass all unit tests. What is `pass@3`? (Three decimals.)

You switch from ROUGE to dense embedding cosine similarity (and BERTScore) to score support answers. Now "Your warranty does NOT cover water damage" scores 0.94 against "Your warranty covers water damage." Why?

When computing ROC-AUC as a pairwise ranking probability over a model outputting quantized buckets (`0.1`, `0.5`, `0.9`), how must tied positive-negative scores be scored, and what fails if ties are broken by row order?

A translation candidate has c = 6 words against a reference of r = 12 words, achieving geometric mean n-gram precision 0.80. Using BLEU's brevity penalty `exp(1 - r/c)` for `c < r`, what is the final BLEU score (0 to 1 scale)? (Three decimals.)
An eval scorer assigns scores `0.8` and `0.5` to two positive items, and `0.7`, `0.5`, `0.2` to three negative items. Counting ties as 0.5, what is the exact ROC-AUC?

Your RAG summarization score drops from 0.44 ROUGE-L to 0.19 overnight after a model swap, even though human reviewers rate the new summaries slightly better. Neither the reference set nor the prompt changed. What do you inspect?
Why did code-generation benchmarks abandon BLEU and CodeBLEU as primary pass metrics in favor of execution-based `pass@k`, and when can execution scoring itself mislead?
Your coding agent boasts `pass@5 = 88%` on an internal SQL benchmark, yet production users see correct queries on under half of first runs and frequent retries. What scoring fallacy hid this problem?
Design a reference-scoring pipeline for medical-record summarization where missing a medication dose is critical, phrasing varies widely, and 2,000 test cases must run nightly in CI under $15.

Your team wants to replace human reference grading with a semantic LLM-as-judge for open-ended customer emails. How do you validate the judge and choose the calibration metric before turning off human scoring?

A support agent can read incoming external emails, query the internal customer billing database, and call an outbound `send_webhook` tool. Why is this combination high-risk even if the model has safety training?
Why must an autonomous agent's step count, dollar spend, and wall-clock timeout be enforced by deterministic harness code outside the model rather than instructed in the system prompt?

An autonomous workflow executes 15 sequential tool steps without mid-run human recovery. Each step independently succeeds with probability 0.94. What percentage of full 15-step runs finish without any step failure? (One decimal.)

Your coding agent runs bash commands with `subprocess.run(cmd, shell=True, timeout=10)`. When the agent spawns a background server (`python server.py & sleep 60`), `subprocess.run` raises `TimeoutExpired`, yet container CPU stays pinned at 100%. Why?
Compare OS-level namespace jails (`bwrap`), user-space kernel containers (`gVisor`), and hardware MicroVMs (`Firecracker`) for executing agent-generated code. When is `bwrap` insufficient?

A bounded agent loop allows up to 12 turns. Each turn appends 1,500 tokens of tool output to a 3,000-token initial prompt (turn 1 sends 3,000 input tokens, turn 2 sends 4,500, etc.) and ignores prompt caching. How many total input tokens are billed across a full 12-turn run?

Your autonomous coding agent has a hard 25-turn limit, yet logs show it oscillating 12 times between editing `router.py` (breaking `handler.py`) and reverting `router.py` (breaking `handler.py` imports) until turn 25 expires. What guard is missing?

A finance-ops agent answers questions about customer invoices and issues refunds up to $50. Today it uses one shared admin Postgres role and a generic `run_sql` tool. Redesign the permission boundary.

An orchestrator sets a $2.00 limit per user request, yet allows spawning sub-agents with an independent $2.00 cap each up to depth 3 (1 root orchestrator spawns 3 level-1 sub-agents, and each level-1 spawns 3 level-2 sub-agents). What is the worst-case spend for one request if caps are not shared?

Your single-agent coding loop ends every edit by prompting itself "Double-check that your patch satisfies all edge cases and tests pass." Logs show it approves 96% of its own broken patches without running `pytest`. Why, and what fixes it?

Design a bounded-autonomy approval flow for an enterprise infrastructure agent that proposes Terraform changes, waits up to 24 hours for human sign-off, and guarantees the approved plan matches what executes.

Your agent connects to third-party MCP tool servers to read tickets and update Jira. How do you enforce bounded autonomy against rug-pull tool description updates, oversized tool outputs, and argument injection?

A healthcare chatbot runs a PII redaction guardrail only on the LLM's output before showing text to the patient. Why is relying solely on an output guardrail insufficient when calling a third-party model API?
Your input safety guardrail achieves 99% recall on prompt attacks and a 4% false-positive rate on normal support queries. Why is this a severe product bug, and how do you measure and tune it?

A financial assistant serves 200,000 requests/day. Real attacks are 0.5% of traffic (1,000 requests) and benign traffic is 99.5% (199,000 requests). Your input guardrail achieves 95% true-positive rate on attacks and a 2% false-positive rate on benign queries. How many benign user requests are wrongly blocked per day?

During a traffic spike, your external guardrail classifier starts timing out after 500 ms. A developer sets `fail_open: true` globally on the API gateway. What fails in production, and when is `fail_open` the wrong default?
Why do output guardrails conflict with low-latency token streaming, and how do production gateways resolve that tension without buffering the entire response?

A system guards against indirect prompt injection using three independent defense layers: input delimiter plus classifier (catches 70% of attacks), tool-argument validator (catches 80% of remaining), and outbound domain allowlist (catches 90% of remaining). What percentage of attacks succeed past all three layers? (One decimal.)

A new prompt and guardrail update rolls out as a 5% canary on 80,000 uniform daily requests, checked every 15-minute window before auto-rollback triggers. If a bug causes 12% of canary responses to emit unsafe text, how many unsafe responses occur in one 15-minute window before rollback?

Your input guardrail blocks exact banned phrases and regex PII patterns cleanly in unit tests, yet red-teamers bypass it using zero-width spaces, base64 strings, or visually identical Cyrillic letters (`а` for `a`). Why, and what fixes the mismatch?

When an output guardrail fires in production, returning a blunt `"I cannot help with that"` breaks downstream callers or leaks which rule triggered. Compare the four response policies when a guardrail triggers and when to use each.

After enabling a strict faithfulness/grounding guardrail on a RAG assistant, useful answers drop 22% because the guardrail flags harmless connective reasoning ("Because your plan renewed in March...") as unsupported hallucinations. How do you debug and recalibrate this?
Design a guardrail pipeline for a high-throughput enterprise assistant with a strict 150 ms guardrail latency budget, where full LLM-as-judge checks take 700 ms synchronously.

Red-teamers bypass your single-turn input guardrail by spreading a prohibited request across six innocent-looking conversation turns. How do you design stateful guardrails without blowing latency or context limits?
When a model generates tokens one at a time for a single user, what limits its speed on a GPU?
A 7B model in bf16 (14 GB of weights) runs on a GPU with 2 TB/s of memory bandwidth. What's the theoretical maximum decode speed for one sequence? (Tokens per second.)
Same GPU, same model, but quantised to int4 weights (3.5 GB). What's the new ceiling for one sequence?
With 32 layers, 8 KV heads of dimension 128, and bf16 (2 bytes), how much KV cache does one token take? (KiB.)
How much KV cache does one sequence with an 8,192-token context need? (GiB.)
After loading the weights, 40 GiB of GPU memory is left for the KV cache. How many 8k-token sequences can run at once?
Why do most recent open models use grouped-query attention (GQA)?
With static batching, a batch of 16 requests finishes only when the longest answer finishes. What does continuous batching change?
Users say answers take a long time to *start*, but once text appears it streams quickly. Which metric is bad, and what are the usual fixes?
Every request starts with the same 3,000-token system prompt. Which optimisation targets that directly?

In speculative decoding, a small draft model proposes 4 tokens and the large model checks them in one pass. Each draft token is accepted with probability 0.8, independently, and checking stops at the first rejection. On average, how many tokens does each pass of the large model produce? (Two decimals.)
With temperature 0 in production, the same prompt sometimes gets slightly different answers. What's the usual explanation?
A support bot must answer from a policy manual that changes every week. Fine-tune, or use RAG?
What does LoRA train?
LoRA with rank 16 on one 4,096 × 4,096 projection matrix. How many trainable parameters does that add?
As a percentage of that matrix's 16,777,216 parameters, how many does the rank-16 adapter train? (Percent, three decimals.)
What does QLoRA add on top of LoRA?
You fine-tune on 10,000 examples averaging 1,500 tokens each, for 3 epochs. How many training tokens is that, in millions?
After fine-tuning on 5,000 legal Q&A pairs, the model is great at legal questions but worse at general instructions and basic maths. What happened, and what helps?
Validation loss on your fine-tuning data keeps going down, but when people try the model, its answers are getting worse. What's the likely gap?
A fine-tuned chat model works in your training notebook but produces rambling text when served. What do you check first?
How does DPO differ from RLHF with PPO?
You can fine-tune on 1,000 examples carefully written by experts, or on 100,000 scraped Q&A pairs of mixed quality. For teaching an instruction-following style, which is usually better?
Your production extraction service calls the provider's floating `model-latest` alias rather than a pinned dated snapshot. Why is this risky even when API uptime is 100%?
When should you choose a specialized 8B model (or fine-tuned encoder) over a frontier reasoning model in a production system?

A two-tier router serves 1,000,000 monthly requests averaging 1,000 input tokens and 300 output tokens each. It sends 70% of requests to a fast tier ($0.15/1M input, $0.60/1M output) and 30% to a frontier tier ($3.00/1M input, $15.00/1M output), while the router classifier adds $0.02 per 1,000 requests. What is the total monthly spend in USD?
Compare an upfront predictive router against a sequential confidence cascade. When does a cascade lose both latency and cost against direct frontier calls?

Sending a request directly to a frontier model costs $0.020. A cascade instead runs a small model ($0.002) plus an external verifier ($0.002) on every request, then escalates failing cases to the frontier model ($0.020). What is the maximum escalation rate (in percent) where the cascade still stays cheaper than calling the frontier model directly?

Your two-tier cascade uses a small model with a prompt asking it to rate its own certainty (1–5) and escalates scores below 4. Monthly cost drops 55%, yet wrong answers on subtle policy edge cases jump while escalation stays at 12%. Why?

On a 2,000-query golden benchmark, a tuned routing threshold sends 1,400 queries to the fast tier (where the fast tier achieves 88.0% accuracy) and 600 queries to the frontier tier (where the frontier tier achieves 95.0% accuracy). What is the router's blended accuracy in percent?

A chat coding assistant runs a per-turn router: greetings go to an 8B model and debugging turns go to a 70B model. Users report abrupt tone and formatting whiplash across turns, and provider prompt-cache hit rates sit near zero on long threads. What went wrong, and how do you fix it?

Why do static leaderboard ranks (like overall MMLU or Arena Elo) fail as the sole model-selection criterion in an enterprise agent router, and what capability signals belong in the routing matrix instead?

You add a new fast model to a production semantic router. Aggregate p50 latency drops 30% and spend drops 25%, yet checkout conversion in French and German drops 14% with zero HTTP errors. How do you isolate and resolve this?
Design a multi-region LLM routing gateway serving US, EU, and APAC users where EU prompts must stay strictly inside EU endpoints under data residency rules while minimizing global tail latency.
Design an online contextual-bandit router that learns model selection weights from live production feedback without starving newly added models or chasing delayed labels blindly.
When your primary frontier LLM times out on a RAG product-search assistant, what is the right graceful degradation order rather than immediately returning HTTP 500?

A primary model provider delivers 99.0% availability (0.99), and an independent secondary provider delivers 98.0% availability (0.98). Assuming instant health failover on outage, what is the combined theoretical availability in percent?
Explain the Closed, Open, and Half-Open states of a circuit breaker on an LLM gateway, and clarify why a breaker does not repair a failing model server.

Your LLM gateway's circuit breaker suddenly trips Open during a busy afternoon, dropping healthy requests to a degraded fallback—yet upstream GPU health checks are 100% green. Logs show a surge of `HTTP 400` and guardrail rejection responses from malformed client payloads. What bug triggered the false trip?

To cut tail latency, your gateway sends a hedged backup call to a secondary endpoint whenever the primary model has not returned a first token by its p95 latency mark (affecting 5% of traffic). On 200,000 daily requests costing $0.006 per dispatched call (with no partial billing refund on late abort), what extra daily spend in USD does hedging add?

During recovery from a provider outage, all 40 gateway pods exit their 30-second Open cooldown simultaneously in Half-Open state, each allowing 5 probe requests through—instantly crashing the warming upstream vLLM cluster again. Diagnose and fix this.
Under severe upstream GPU saturation, why is strict priority-based load shedding (rejecting background batch jobs first) better than keeping FIFO queues or dropping 20% of all requests at random?

A RAG pipeline serves 100,000 daily requests with 99.5% primary upstream availability (500 primary failures/day). When the primary generator fails, a graceful fallback serves cached answers or BM25 document cards for 76% of failed requests, leaving 24% visibly failing. What is user-visible availability in percent?

During a primary API outage, traffic fails over cleanly to a backup open-weight model hosted elsewhere—with HTTP 200s across the board—yet downstream JSON parsers crash on 18% of requests and tool calls loop. What failed across the failover boundary?

During a vector-database timeout on a medical benefits assistant, an engineer suggests falling back to pure LLM generation without context so users still get a fast answer. Why is that dangerous, and what degraded path should you build instead?
Design an automated brownout controller for an enterprise AI research assistant when GPU cluster utilization exceeds 92% or error-budget burn spikes 5×.

Design active-passive regional failover for a stateful conversational AI API when Region A loses all GPU capacity. Address in-flight streams, conversation history, prompt-cache warmness, and preventing Region B overload.

You set a rate limit of 60 requests per minute using a simple fixed calendar-minute counter (`minute_key`). Why can a client still hit your GPU inference server with 120 requests inside a 2-second burst?

A tenant's token bucket has a maximum capacity of 120,000 tokens and refills steadily at 2,000 tokens/second (120,000 TPM). Starting from full capacity, a script fires 15 requests consuming 6,000 tokens each immediately, waits 10 seconds, and then fires 10 more requests of 6,000 tokens each (admitted one by one). How many requests in the second wave are rejected with HTTP 429?
Why do modern LLM providers exempt or heavily discount cached input tokens against Tokens-Per-Minute (TPM) rate limits, and what breaks if your internal gateway fails to mirror that distinction?

Your product sets an end-to-end p99 latency budget of 1,000 ms for the first token in a RAG assistant. Sequential pipeline stages consume: 25 ms gateway auth/WAF, 45 ms query embedding, 190 ms hybrid vector search plus cross-encoder rerank, 120 ms output safety buffer, and 40 ms network round-trip. What maximum TTFT budget (in ms) remains for the LLM call?

Your internal FinOps gateway tracks a tenant's cumulative input tokens against their monthly cap and shows them at 35% usage—yet the provider invoice arrives at 3.2× the tenant's budget. What billing oversight caused this?

A workflow orchestrator enforces a 400 ms per-call timeout and fans out 12 independent retrieval/scoring calls in parallel per request. Why does p99 end-to-end latency spike far above 400 ms, and how does deadline propagation fix it?

An engineering org enforces a $1,200/day hard cap across three teams. Each team has a $400/day soft quota and may burst up to 25% above its soft quota ($500) only while total org spend stays below $1,200. On Tuesday, Team A spends $400 and Team B spends $350. What is the maximum daily spend in USD Team C can reach before throttling?
